thread:
incident-bot: P1 Alert: kv-cache reuse correctness detector (stale-key-detect) tripped across us-west-2 runtime cluster. Impact: context mixing / wrong-seq-offsets observed. Auto-pager routed to oncall. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/kv-cache

maya: ack. Noticing a spike in incorrect completions from production logs and a customer slack. Posting sample traces.

adrian: I'm taking this. Paging kai and anya for runtime + repro help. Initial read: regression in the reuse path where cached slot validation skipped for micro-batched continuous flows. Leads to stale KV pages being attached to new requests with mismatching seq ranges.

kai: Confirmed in tracing. Affected nodes: runtime-22..runtime-27 (us-west-2). Many traces show reused_kv_seq=201 but request expected start_seq>=220.

anya: We have three inbound reports: two customers reported garbled dialog tokens, one internal e2e detected mismatched embeddings. Treating as data-correctness P1.

adrian: Live mitigations (immediate): 1) flip feature flag: kv_reuse_enabled=false on us-west-2 cluster 2) set continuous_batch.concurrency_limit=1 for affected pools 3) trigger targeted kv-evict for nodes 22..27 4) notify CS.

maya: Commands to run (ops):
```
# disable reuse for specific pool
POST /ops-api/flags {"flag":"kv_reuse_enabled","value":false,"scope":"us-west-2:gpu-cluster"}

# throttle continuous batch concurrency
POST /ops-api/configs {"key":"continuous_batch.concurrency_limit","value":1,"scope":"us-west-2:gpu-cluster"}

# targeted evict
POST /ops-api/kv/evict {"nodes":["runtime-22","runtime-23","runtime-24","runtime-25","runtime-26","runtime-27"]}
```
ops-bot: Running flag change job id job-8844. Evict job job-8845 queued.

kai: Applying flags now. Will monitor. Rolling restarts are avoided where possible.

adrian: Evidence snippet from runtime logs (compressed):
```
[2026-02-03T14:12:10Z] node=runtime-23 req=px-998 cache_hit=true cached.seq=201 cached.last_ts=2026-02-03T14:11:58Z request.start_seq=223 -> seq_mismatch
[2026-02-03T14:12:10Z] node=runtime-23 req=px-999 postwrite cached.seq=223
[2026-02-03T14:12:11Z] node=runtime-23 req=px-998 resumed_cached.seq=201 -> produced tokens referencing other session
```
This pattern repeats with sub-millisecond interleaving.

anya: Repro steps: run continuous-batching harness with a mix of short token queries and a few long decoder streams, with batch interleaving rate >50rps. The bug surfaces when the eviction/validation race allows a previously used KV page to be assigned without verifying the current request's start_seq. Added repro in incident repo: github.com/redwood/incidents/kv-repro/us-west-2-2166001234.

maya: Quick note: we'll keep the cluster disabled for reuse until we have a tested fix. Also add a temporary rate limiting rule for customers with high QPS to prevent recurrence.

ops-bot: job-8844: kv_reuse_enabled=false applied to us-west-2 on hosts runtime-22..27. job-8845: eviction started.

cs-liaison: CS update: impacted customers flagged: orbit-ads (context leakage in ad-generation), ledgercorp (two API calls with mixed context), and internal analytics team. Drafting outreach.

adrian: Hotfix plan: add strict sequence validation gate and a fast-path fallback that refuses reuse when cached.seq < request.start_seq OR cached.last_seen_age > 3s. Also add unit test that simulates micro-batch interleaving. Branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/hotfix/kv-seq-guard (PR #6432).

kai: Suggest small-scope code change plus backstop: also add an assert in the reuse allocator to log and drop reuse if mismatch detected in prod. That will give us telemetry while avoiding silent corruption. I'll add that to PR.

maya: Ops suggestion: instead of immediate code push, keep flag off and run canary validation for 15m after eviction. If stable, merge PR and go through expedited deploy.

ops-bot: eviction job job-8845 completed. Confirmed KV pages cleared on runtime-22..27.

maya: Initial metric: incorrect-output alerts decreased 92% within 90s of mitigation. Error traces still occasional from older requests; monitoring for 10m.

anya: Working on unit/integration tests now. Will include a failing scenario that reproduces the seq mismatch and a fix that ensures allocator checks both seq window and last_seen timestamp before reuse.

adrian: Handing off to kai to drive the fix and patch rollout. I'll coordinate postmortem.

kai: Taking ownership. Timeline: land PR in 30-45m, canary deploy to runtime-27, run 200k interleaved e2e, then progressive roll to runtime-22..26 with 3m observation windows.

cs-liaison: Customer messages drafted. Legal reviewed. We'll offer affected customers log exports and a short technical call.

maya: Additional mitigation: add a short-term telemetry spike rule to raise priority on any trace showing reused.seq < request.start_seq so we can catch stragglers.

ops-bot: telemetry rule created id rule-77.

kai: PR opened #6432. CI: linux+integration green; flaky mac unrelated. Requesting expedited code owner review from adrian and maya.

adrian: Reviewing PR. Also pin the regression to commit 7c12a5 (continuous-batcher reuse path) in the incident notes.

maya: Note for postmortem: capture reproducer steps, timeline, customer impact, rollback decisions, and a recommendation to add stricter pre-reuse validation in allocator plus better canary gating for future reuse optimizations.

ops-bot: state update: mitigations applied, active monitoring. Next update in 45m or on change.

kai: Quick status: telemetry indicates near-zero incorrect outputs after eviction and flags. Proceeding to validate PR on runtime-27 canary now.

anya: I'll validate post-merge and run the harness against canary. If green, proceed with staged rollout.

cs-liaison: Sending customer emails now. Will track replies and escalate high-severity customers to engineering if they request immediate investigation.

adrian: Thanks team. I'll start the postmortem doc and schedule the follow-up RCA. Leaving primary to kai for the rollout.

incident-bot: INCIDENT state=mitigated (active-monitoring). Will resolve after stable metrics for 60m and successful e2e run.
